Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Build an invoicing system incrementally over multiple requests. House rules: all money as integer cents (use roundCents()), never throw (use fail() from result.js), never mutate arguments (return new objects/arrays), run npm test before declaring done.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Money handling: all amounts in cents (integers), with roundCents() for fractional results
   - Result pattern: { ok: true, value: X } or { ok: false, error: CODE }
   - Invoice lifecycle: draft → issued → partially_paid or paid
   - Discount types: line-level (absolute %), tier-based (automatic, silver/gold/standard), vouchers (fixed amount post-VAT)
   - VAT: calculated per-line on amount after discount, rounded per line, summed for invoice
   - Payment terms: NET14 (14 days), NET30 (30 days, default), EOM (end of month)
   - Customer ID normalization: trim whitespace and uppercase for consistency
   - Date arithmetic: all in UTC, never local timezone

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/invoices.js: Core invoice engine with:
     - createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines, terms='NET30' }) - returns ok({ customerId, issueDate, status: 'draft', terms, dueDate, lines })
     - lineTotal(line) - returns qty * unitPrice
     - lineDiscount(line) - returns line total * discountPercent / 100 (rounded)
     - lineVat(line) - returns vatRate% of (lineTotal - lineDiscount), rounded
     - invoiceTotals(invoice) - returns { subtotal, discount, vat, voucher, total } where total = subtotal - discount + vat - voucher
     - addLine(invoice, { sku, qty, discountPercent }) - adds line to draft, applies tier discount if not explicit
     - removeLine(invoice, sku) - removes line from draft, prevents removing last line
     - issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers) - assigns number, sets status='issued'
     - applyVoucher(invoice, { code, amount }) - IN PROGRESS: to add { code, amount } to invoice.voucher on draft only
   
   - src/customers.js: Customer lookup and tier management
     - TIER_DISCOUNTS = { gold: 5, silver: 2.5, standard: 0 }
     - normalizeId(id) - returns String(id).trim().toUpperCase()
     - getCustomer(id) - normalizes id before lookup, returns ok(customer) or fail('CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND')
   
   - src/catalogue.js: Product lookup (pre-existing, used by invoices)
     - getProduct(sku) - returns ok(product) with { sku, name, unitPrice, vatRate } or fail('UNKNOWN_SKU')
   
   - src/dates.js: Date utilities
     - isValidDate(text) - validates YYYY-MM-DD format, checks real dates in UTC, rejects impossible dates (Feb 30, etc)
     - addDays(date, n) - returns new date string, handles month/year boundaries
     - daysBetween(a, b) - returns integer days from a to b (b - a)
     - calculateDueDate(issueDate, terms) - returns due date for NET14/NET30/EOM or null if invalid terms
   
   - src/payments.js: Payment recording
     - balanceDue(invoice) - returns max(0, total - sum of payments)
     - recordPayment(invoice, { amount, date }) - adds payment to invoice.payments array, updates status to 'paid' or 'partially_paid'
   
   - src/errors.js: Error codes (all added incrementally):
     - AMOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_INVALID, CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DATE_INVALID, DISCOUNT_INVALID
     - LINE_NOT_FOUND, NO_LINES, NOT_DRAFT, NOT_ISSUED, OVERPAYMENT
     - QTY_INVALID, TERMS_INVALID, UNKNOWN_SKU, VOUCHER_EXISTS (just added)

   - src/render.js: Plain-text invoice rendering with lineItem and VAT details
   - test/invoices.test.js: 114 tests covering invoice creation, discounts, VAT, tier discounts, ID normalization, terms

   - test/payments.test.js: 14 tests covering payment recording and balance calculation
   - Total: 159 tests passing

Fixed by updating all test assertions to match the new return format each time: first { subtotal, total }, then added discount -> { subtotal, discount, total }, then added vat -> { subtotal, discount, vat, total }, finally added voucher (in progress).
   - Test expected daysBetween('2025-01-01', '2025-12-31') = 363 but got 364. Fixed test expectation: 365-day year means 364 days between Jan 1 and Dec 31.
   - Test used require() in ES module which threw ReferenceError. Fixed by importing invoiceTotals directly at top of test file.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Learned date edge cases: leap years, month boundaries, EOM calculation for Feb vs 31-day months
   - Discovered that explicit discountPercent of 0 should suppress tier discount (line exists without discountPercent property)
   - Handled status transitions correctly: 'issued' -> 'partially_paid' (on first partial payment) -> 'paid' (when balance reaches 0)
